items.title: Publish fake stats, get cited in LLMs
items.summary: Researchers found that publishing fabricated statistics can lead to their citation in large language models (LLMs), highlighting the importance of maintaining accuracy in academic and scientific communications. This issue underscores potential biases and inaccuracies that can propagate through AI systems if not properly addressed.
items.summary_detailed: Researchers fabricated statistical data and published it in an academic paper, only to find that these false statistics were later used and cited by various large language models (LLMs), highlighting the potential risks of misinformation propagation through AI systems. The involved parties include the researchers who created the fake data and the developers of LLMs like Anthropic, Alibaba Cloud, Google, and Meta. This incident underscores the broader impact on scientific integrity and the need for robust fact-checking mechanisms in AI training datasets.
items.summary_bullets:
• Researchers published fabricated statistics.
• The false data was included in academic papers.
• Language models cited the incorrect information.
• It highlights the importance of fact-checking.

items.title: H2DF: Calibrated Target Bands for Controllable Language-Model Unlearning
items.description:
arXiv:2610.26864v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Gradient ascent (GA) is a simple language-model unlearning baseline, but it continues increasing forget loss after useful forgetting has occurred. This unbounded pressure can damage retained utility and make forgotten examples abnormally high-loss. We
items.summary: A new method called H2DF aims to calibrate target bands for controllable language-model unlearning using gradient ascent (GA), addressing the issue of GA continuing to increase forget loss even after useful forgetting, which can harm retained utility and make forgotten examples overly high-loss. This matters because it provides a more controlled approach to unlearning in language models, potentially improving their overall performance and reliability.
items.summary_detailed: Researchers have developed H2DF, a calibrated target band approach for controllable language-model unlearning that addresses the issue of gradient ascent (GA) continuing to increase forget loss even after useful forgetting has occurred, potentially damaging retained utility and making forgotten examples overly high-loss. This new method involves adjusting target bands during the unlearning process to ensure more controlled and effective forgetting. The broader impact could be improved privacy and security in natural language processing applications by allowing for more precise control over what information a model retains or forgets.
items.summary_bullets:
• GA continues to increase forget loss even after useful forgetting.
• This uncontrolled pressure can harm the retained model's utility.
• Forgotten examples may become unusually high-loss due to over-unlearning.

Abstract: Modern speech systems are evolving into ecosystems of autonomous speech agents that speak together, negotiate, and trade assets such as embeddings, spectrograms, or raw data. In such markets, sellers cannot reveal assets for evaluation due to privacy
items.summary: WaveCommitments introduces private and verifiable speech-agent marketplaces where sellers can evaluate assets without revealing them, crucial for maintaining privacy in evolving speech ecosystems that involve autonomous agents trading various types of data. The broader impact could revolutionize how speech technologies are developed and utilized by ensuring privacy and verifiability in asset trading.
